blocks.heading: Pesach as the first stage, and the kares of chametz

paragraphs.text: The Rav opens with the principle that the Yamim Tovim rise in level: Pesach is the first glimpse of the Chassan, Shavuos the betrothal, Sukkos the full union. Pesach is lesser: the full Hallel is said only on its first day, and chametz, which the Tanya calls klipah that must first be elevated, cannot yet be eaten, while on Shavuos the offering is chametz.

Yet chametz on Pesach carries kares, unlike the prohibitions of Shavuos and Sukkos. The Rav explains that kares cuts a vessel binding a Jew to Hashem, and its opposite is kashrus: whoever eats matzah binds himself to Hashem in a way no other Yom Tov offers.

blocks.heading: Reishis, renewal and the joy of Nisan

paragraphs.text: Pesach, the Rav continues, is the reishis, the Rosh Hashanah of the festivals as the Mishnah says, and a beginning holds everything in potential. It is a renewal, 'hachodesh hazeh lachem': the first contact with Hashem, which changes a Jew's very essence.

What happens in Heaven comes down to earth. The tzeruf of the Name for Nisan is drawn from 'Yismechu hashamayim vesagel ha'aretz': because there is joy above over the new nation, the Kallah of Hashem, nature wakes up: trees bud, ice melts, birds return singing. Shlomo HaMelech caught this theme of Nisan in Shir Hashirim, the song of Chassan and Kallah, a parable for Hashem and Klal Yisrael.

The Rav brings the Rema's tradition that techiyas hameisim will come on Pesach through a dew of life, and that is the tal we begin asking for on Pesach. So it is a time for every Jew to make a reckoning and become a new person, casting off the shrouds of the yetzer hara. The same newness appears in the custom of new clothes, dishes and fresh paint for Pesach.

Pesach is the key to the year, and the matzah is a key. To explain matzah the Rav begins with bread: the Shulchan Aruch notes that Hamotzi has ten words, for bread contains the ten utterances of creation. Every creature embodies a trait, a sheep chesed and a lion gevurah, but man, created last as Rashi says, holds them all, with one dominant.

Hence a person prefers certain foods yet needs variety, while bread, containing everything, never tires him. That holiness reaches only one who eats properly; one who bites into bread without a bracha, like Esav in Parshas Toldos, eats klipah. The poskim add that the ten words also match the ten sefiros and the ten mitzvos tied to bread.

blocks.heading: The Malbim: how a Jew eats

paragraphs.text: The Rav tells that the Malbim, a Rav in a German city full of maskilim, once debated a group of them. Afterward he said that they know much, but he knows how to eat: he wakes hungry, yet first washes negel vasser, dresses, davens, washes and dips the bread in salt.
Bread, he adds, carries a threefold holiness, like the Torah given in three parts, as the Gemara in Shabbos says: lechem equals three times the Name, 78, and feeds the soul.

Matzah is higher still: it is the food of the perfect Adam. The Rav spells the Name in full, yud-vav-dalet, hei-aleph, vav-aleph-vav, hei-aleph, reaching 45, the value of Adam and of 'Mah'. On Pesach this holiness descends from a world so high it is called Mah, beyond understanding, the source of Yetzias Mitzrayim.

That is why the Seder opens with a child's question: one can only ask. Bread is three times 26, but matzah is three times 45, 135, the key to that world, which is why matzah is eaten three times at the Seder.

blocks.heading: The key of birth and opening

paragraphs.text: Yetzias Mitzrayim was a birth: a new nation came forth from within another nation like a child from the womb. The Gemara says Hashem keeps three keys Himself, including birth and techiyas hameisim, and on Pesach every Jew is reborn through the matzah, the key Hashem entrusts to no one.

Hence 'peter rechem' was commanded on Pesach, and Targum Onkelos renders matzah 'patira', opening. Opening the aron, the Zohar says, is a time of favor, with Brich Shmei; so too the matzah opens, and Hashem says 'pischi li', open up for Me.

blocks.heading: Tal, the matzah capsule and the open door

paragraphs.text: The passuk continues that His head is filled with tal. The Rav explains tal, 39, as the first three letters of the Name in full spelling, descending to the final hei, Klal Yisrael, and that hei is the matzah.

Thus the Ba'al HaTanya explains 'Ha lachma anya': the flour and water are only a capsule, and inside is the same light the Jews ate in Mitzrayim, the original and not a copy. After the matzah the door is opened for Eliyahu HaNavi, the angel of geulah, for all of Pesach is an opening.

blocks.heading: Tefillah for the King, re'iyah, and wanting geulah

paragraphs.text: The Rav calls the day Rosh Hashanah for kings, when new appointments over nations and blessings are made in Heaven, and says one should daven that Hashem alone be King, with Mashiach as His chariot. He brings the Avnei Nezer that on every Yom Tov the soul somehow comes to Yerushalayim for re'iyah.

Citing the Gemara in Chagigah, he says that as Hashem shows Himself in full glory, a Jew should present himself in completeness. Pesach's gift is geulah, yet, the Midrash says, most Jews in Mitzrayim, who did not want it, died. So a Jew must want release from the yetzer hara; otherwise Yom Tov passes dry, without the 'birkas mo'adecha' of its tefillah.
